body:
Got an old phone in a drawer? It could be a Unity Node.

A Unity Node is a phone that quietly helps run a decentralised network — a DePIN — and gets paid for the work it does. No mining, no fancy hardware: an Android or iPhone, the Unity Nodes app, and a free licence from us.

Nodes currently earn around $0.10–$0.50 per device per day — that scales with network demand, so today's numbers aren't guaranteed.

Get the app: worlddepin.io/app · Free licence: worlddepin.io · hello@worlddepin.io

Starting a Unity Node takes about five minutes:

1. Request a free licence at worlddepin.io — we email your lease code.
2. Install the Unity Nodes app (worlddepin.io/app — Android and iPhone).
3. Sign in as a License Operator and paste in the code. Done — the node activates itself.

No sign-up hoops. You request a licence on our site, the lease code lands in your inbox, and the app takes it from there. If you get stuck on any step, reply to the email and a human walks you through it.

Which phones work? Any reasonably modern Android or iPhone with the Unity Nodes app. We've seen everything from a Nokia C300 to a Pixel 8 Pro running as nodes. The phone doesn't need a SIM for the basic Connection task.

Your lease code is held for 14 days. If a code isn't activated in that time it goes back into the pool for someone else — so once it lands, give yourself five minutes and get the node running. We'll nudge you after a week if it's still waiting.

Uptime tip #1 (Android): battery optimisation is the number-one reason nodes go quiet. Settings → Apps → Unity Nodes → Battery → Unrestricted. Takes ten seconds, makes all the difference.

Get the app: worlddepin.io/app · Free licence: worlddepin.io · hello@worlddepin.io

Uptime tip #2 (iPhone): keep the app open in the background and Background App Refresh on for Unity Nodes. iOS is stricter than Android about background work — the guide at worlddepin.io/uptime has the exact settings.

Get the app: worlddepin.io/app · Free licence: worlddepin.io · hello@worlddepin.io

Uptime tip #3: a dedicated charger and a stable Wi-Fi spot beat everything else. A node that never leaves the shelf is a node that never drops off the network.

Get the app: worlddepin.io/app · Free licence: worlddepin.io · hello@worlddepin.io

Uptime tip #4 (Samsung): One UI has its own sleeping-apps list on top of Android's battery settings. Make sure Unity Nodes is in 'never sleeping apps' or it'll be put to sleep overnight. Full walkthrough: worlddepin.io/uptime

Get the app: worlddepin.io/app · Free licence: worlddepin.io · hello@worlddepin.io
